title: Measurable functions, simple functions and the integral
summary: Measurable functions and their closure properties; simple functions and approximation; the integral of nonnegative functions; monotone convergence and Fatou.

objectives.description: Construct increasing simple approximations to a nonnegative measurable function.
Define the nonnegative Lebesgue integral independently of a chosen representation.
Use monotone convergence and Fatou's lemma, and diagnose invalid interchanges of limit and integral.

preparation.description: Read Lectures 9–11 of the 18.102 Spring 2021 notes.

activities.title: Lecture and exact source reading
activities.instructions: Work through the prepared lecture together with its named source sections. Reconstruct the displayed derivations before looking back. The source reading is part of this unit, including the proof obligations identified in the notes.

activities.title: Problem sheet and discussion
activities.instructions: Write an independent attempt at each problem. Use one hint at a time if needed; preserve the original attempt and record what assistance changed. Explain the hypotheses aloud before requesting a step check.

activities.title: Return without the scaffolding
activities.instructions: After a gap, reconstruct the central argument without notes and revisit the transfer or synthesis problem. Compare against your previous work only afterwards. Record what remains unresolved; reading or recall alone does not certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to sample the listed objectives. Give an independent account of the main theorem and its hypotheses, and solve the transfer/synthesis task. An accepted single exercise is evidence only for its tested capabilities, not whole-unit mastery.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A pointwise limit of Riemann integrable functions must remain Riemann integrable.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Indicators of increasing finite sets can converge to the Dirichlet function. Lebesgue measurability, unlike Riemann integrability, is stable under measurable pointwise limits.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Pointwise convergence permits exchanging limit and integral.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Monotone convergence needs an increasing nonnegative sequence; Fatou gives only an inequality without stronger control.
